subject: Nuclear fusion
hook: NUCLEAR FUSION IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Nuclear fusion's most favorable reaction, deuterium-tritium (DT) fusion, was not initially assumed to be the best path; it was only discovered to be 100 times more reactive than other methods due to a resonance enhancement discovered years after research began.
angle_support: Theoretical assumptions about DT fusion gave it a similar cross-section to DD.
However, in 1946 Egon Bretscher discovered a resonance enhancement giving the DT reaction a cross-section ~100 times larger.
title: The Accidental Discovery Behind Modern Nuclear Fusion
description: Scientists once believed fusing deuterium with tritium offered no practical advantage over other fuels. An unexpected laboratory finding in 1946 completely transformed atomic research. This hidden nuclear property made one specific combination the foundation for modern power concepts.
narration: NUCLEAR FUSION IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture physicists immediately knowing the golden fuel recipe. In reality, early researchers assumed blending deuterium and tritium offered no real advantage over plain deuterium. Theorists predicted both pairings would perform identically. That changed in 1946 when Egon Bretscher measured the interaction. He discovered a nuclear resonance enhancement that made the combination roughly one hundred times more reactive than expected, turning a dismissed match into fusion's primary path. The premier fuel of future energy was once deemed completely ordinary.
